title: Persist the cancelled order state
summary: Maps the cancelled state, adds the database migration, and verifies round-trip persistence.

nodes.description: Extend persistence for the cancelled state and verify its database round trip.

rationale: Persistence is isolated from the domain transition so the mapping and migration can be reviewed independently from the business rule.

decisions.summary: Keep storing order state as its string name.
decisions.rationale: This matches the existing mapping and makes the new Cancelled value backward-compatible without renumbering enum values.

alternatives.approach: Rely on the existing string column accepting the new value without a migration.
alternatives.reasonRejected: The database check constraint enumerates allowed values and must be updated.

failedAttempts.approach: Run dotnet ef migrations add from the API project.
failedAttempts.outcome: The command could not locate the design-time OrdersDbContext.
failedAttempts.lesson: Run migrations with Orders.Infrastructure as the target project and Orders.Api as the startup project.

risks.summary: Application instances using Cancelled must not start before the constraint migration is applied.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing migrate-before-deploy release step.

validation.summary: Confirms a cancelled order can be saved and loaded.
Verified that the migration only extends the allowed state constraint.
